battle.name: 柏壁之戰
battle.brief: 武德二年十一月，秦王李世民率軍出龍門，踏冰渡黃河，屯兵絳州柏壁，與劉武周部將宋金剛相持。唐軍閉營養銳，遣騎斷其糧道，待宋軍糧盡退兵，追至雀鼠谷，一日八戰皆捷。宋金剛退保介休，城西列陣七里，世民遣兵先出稍卻，誘其全軍進擊，自將騎兵繞出敵後猛襲，宋軍崩潰。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 柏壁之戰的交戰雙方，是唐朝與劉武周建立的割據政權。唐方以關中為根本，李淵自太原起兵、進據長安之後，河東與關中一體的格局是唐的立國前提；武德二年出兵的秦王李世民，是李淵次子，以行軍總管身分統兵，唐廷在戰前一度議定放棄河東，最終准他「假精兵三萬」，由長安出龍門關，經蒲坂一線北向而來。漢方是劉武周在隋末以馬步都尉起兵、聚眾於馬邑與汾州一帶建立的政權，據太原、晉州、絳州三處，與陝北梁師都的梁國互為犄角，並遠結突厥以為外援；漢主劉武周自領大政，用兵之權交給宋金剛，任為西南道大行臺，節制太原、晉、絳諸軍，其下有尉遲恭、尋相、黃子英、王行本、呂崇茂等部將，糧道與城防各有人分掌。兩軍編制相近，皆承隋制：步軍由長矛、刀、盾與弓弩組成，騎兵是戰鬥主力，馬上佩橫刀、操長槊，遠射用弓箭與弩，士卒多著皮甲、兜鍪，唐軍另有明光甲一類銅製護胸作重裝。不同的是分量的消長：漢軍南下之眾號稱三萬餘人，後方卻缺乏蓄積；唐軍以精騎為骨幹，輔以步軍與弩手，並有白毦兵這類精選突擊隊伍。戰前唐廷另遣使遊說劉武周與梁師都，約在河東沙漠斷絕以相接應，此議未成，兵鋒遂全落在河東一線。
countriesEn: The two sides at the Battle of Baipo were the Tang court and the separatist regime raised by Liu Wuzhou. The Tang stood on Guanzhong as its base: after Li Yuan rose at Taiyuan and took Chang'an, the union of Hedong with Guanzhong was the premise of the dynasty's founding. The Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, the second son of Li Yuan, led the army of 619 in the capacity of Director of Marching Operations; the court had briefly considered abandoning Hedong, and in the end granted him thirty thousand picked troops, who left Chang'an by Longmen Pass and came north by way of Puban. On the other side stood the state Liu Wuzhou had built after the fall of Sui, rising as a Commander of Horse and Foot in the marches of Mayi and Fenzhou and gathering a following there; it held Bingzhou, Jinzhou and Jiangzhou, made common cause with the Liang state of Liang Shidu in northern Shaanxi, and looked far north to the Turks for support. Liu Wuzhou himself directed the government and gave the conduct of war to Song Jingang, appointed Director of the Southwest Circuit, who commanded the troops of Bing, Jin and Jiang; under him stood such officers as Yuchi Gong, Xun Xiang, Huang Ziying, Wang Xingben and Lü Chongmao, with men assigned to look after the supply road and the defences. The two armies were organised in much the same way, both following the Sui model: the foot were made up of long spears, sabres, shields, bows and crossbows, while the horse carried the fighting, the rider wearing a horizontal sabre at his side and handling a long lance, shooting with bow and crossbow at range, and the men were commonly in leather armour and helmets, the Tang having in addition heavy troops with the bronze chest protector known as Mingguang armour. What differed was the weight on each side: the Han host that moved south was numbered at more than thirty thousand men but had nothing stored behind it, while the Tang army had picked horse as its backbone, supported by foot and crossbowmen, and units such as the White Guard of picked shock troops. Before the fighting the Tang court also sent envoys to try to win over Liu Wuzhou and Liang Shudu, offering to cut the desert route in Hedong so that the two would support each other; the proposal came to nothing, and the whole weight of the war fell on the Hedong front.
people: 決定此役走向的是秦王李世民。619年太原陷落、關中震駭之際，高祖李淵一度主張放棄河東，李世民上表力爭，說明「太原，王業所基。國之根本；河東富實，京邑所資」，並自請領兵三萬，史載他與劉武周勢不兩立，出師之日高祖親自為他送行。漢方主帥宋金剛，是劉武周倚重的總攬之員，在漢軍中數一數二：他領三萬餘人自太原南下，五月取平遙、六月取介州，兵鋒直指太原，卻在柏壁被唐軍閉營拖住，糧盡而退；介休城西再列陣時仍由他主持，兵敗之後率眾北走上谷，為突厥所擒，遭腰斬。尉遲恭是漢軍最能打的騎將，救援夏縣呂崇茂、奔蒲坂接應王行本，都曾在唐軍側翼撕開缺口，最終在介休隨尋相一同降唐，成為李世民帳下最得力的將領之一，也把北方的騎戰經驗帶進唐軍。尋相與尉遲恭同降，兩人的歸附是此役除地盤之外的另一樁收穫。唐方將佐之中，殷開山、秦叔寶受命於美良川設伏，斬傷漢軍二千餘人；張德政襲殺專司糧道的黃子英，直接斷了漢軍的命脈；李世勣在介休前出，稍卻以誘敵；秦武通取蒲坂，迫王行本出降。此外還有前期一連串敗績留下的名字：張達在榆次外全軍覆沒，姜寶誼、李仲文兩度被俘，裴寂在介休外潰散，李元吉棄晉陽而還。劉武周本人逃入突厥之後，泣對內史令苑君璋說「不用君言，以至於此」，不久仍為突厥所殺。
peopleEn: The man who decided the course of this campaign was the Prince of Qin, Li Shimin. When Taiyuan fell in 619 and Guanzhong was shaken, the founding emperor Li Yuan was for a time in favour of abandoning Hedong; Li Shimin memorialised against it, setting out the reasons plainly: 'Taiyuan is the foundation of the royal enterprise, the root of the state; Hedong is wealthy and rich in produce, and the capital draws its supplies from it.' He asked for thirty thousand picked troops and, as the record has it, swore with Liu Wuzhou that the two would not both live; the emperor himself saw him off when the army marched. The Han commander-in-chief was Song Jingang, the general on whom Liu Wuzhou leaned, and among the Han officers the second to none. He led more than thirty thousand men south out of Bingzhou, took Pingyao in the fifth month and Jiezhou in the sixth, and drove at Taiyuan, only to be held at Baipo by a Tang army that shut its gates and waited him out until his food ran out and he withdrew. He was still the one commanding when the line was formed outside Jiexiu; after that defeat he carried his men north to Shanggu, was taken by the Turks, and was cut in two. Yuchi Gong was the finest fighting horseman of the Han army: he came to the relief of Lü Chongmao at Xiaxian and rode to Puzhang to support Wang Xingben, opening gaps in the Tang flank on both occasions, and in the end at Jiexiu he surrendered with Xun Xiang and became one of the most trusted commanders under Li Shimin, carrying the northern art of mounted fighting into the Tang army. The surrender of Xun Xiang together with Yuchi Gong was the second prize of this campaign besides the ground itself. Among the Tang officers, Yin Kaishan and Qin Shubao were posted to ambush the enemy at Meiliangchuan and cut down more than two thousand Han men; Zhangdezheng struck down Huang Ziying, the officer in charge of the supply road, and so cut the life of the Han army; Li Shiji was put in the van outside Jiexiu and gave ground to draw the enemy; Qin Wutong took Puzhang and forced Wang Xingben to surrender. There are also the names left behind by the run of defeats earlier in the year: Zhang Da was wiped out outside Jiexiu, Jiang Baoyi and Li Zhongwen were taken captive twice, Pei Ji broke up outside Jiezhou, and Li Yuanji abandoned Jinyang and fled. Liu Wuzhou himself, after fleeing into Turkic territory, wept before his Internal Secretary Yuan Junzhang and said, 'I did not take your words, and I came to this'; he was killed by the Turks soon after.
kits: 卡面這件斯巴達長矛並沒有出現在柏壁的戰場上：它是希臘重裝步兵所用的兩米長矛，木製槍身、前端裝鐵矛頭、槍尾套銅，戰士以盾護身、矛為主兵、劍為輔兵，密集方陣前排的刺擊面由它構成。要說它在這場戰役裡的位置，只能說它所代表的「長柄刺擊步兵」譜系在唐軍中是實在的：隋唐軍的步卒長矛，長柄直刺，列在陣前以抗騎兵，正是方陣的骨；唐軍的白毦兵以白衣白毦為號，多持長槊與長刀，在淺水原一役已經衝過敵陣，柏壁追擊戰中精騎突前的作風，是同一支力量延續下來的打法。卡面那句「方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住」，放到柏壁正好有正反兩面：反面是宋金剛在介休城西把陣列到七里，隊形一拉長就斷，長矛的密集刺擊面失去連續，崩潰就從那裡開始；正面是唐軍在雀鼠谷一日八戰，士卒二日未食、三日未解甲，仍能靠縱隊與步騎配合站住陣腳。除長矛與馬槊之外，唐軍的橫刀佩於腰際，供騎手在馬上格鬥與斬擊；弩手與弓箭手在後列覆蓋射界；明光甲這類銅製護胸自漢武以來便是重裝步兵的標誌，兜鍪與皮甲則是普遍裝備。漢軍裝備大體沿用隋制，騎兵的強項在於突厥式的人馬俱備與高速衝擊。攻城器械在柏壁一役的記載裡並不突出，雙方都靠塹壘、封鎖與騎兵擾斷糧道取勝；後勤上，漢軍「軍無蓄積，以虜掠為資」，靠掠奪維持，恰恰是唐軍封鎖策略的要害。馬匹、輜重車與糧秣沿河東官道輸送，太原到柏壁約四百里，柏壁到龍門關一線約七百里，距離本身就是這場戰爭的計算題。
kitsEn: The Spartan long spear on the card never appeared on the field at Baipo: it is the two-metre spear of the Greek heavy infantry, with a wooden shaft, an iron head at the front and a bronze butt-cap at the rear, carried by a warrior who protected himself with a shield, took the spear as his main weapon and the sword as his second, and it was the dense line of thrusting points along the front of the phalanx that the weapon created. Its position in this campaign can only be stated in terms of the tradition it represents: the line of thrusting infantry. In the Sui and Tang armies the foot spear, a long-shafted straight thrust, was ranked at the front to hold off horse, and it was the bone of the formation. The Tang White Guard, marked out by their white coats and white plumes, carried long lances and long sabres, had already broken an enemy line at Qianshuiyuan, and the way picked horse thrust to the front in the pursuit after Baipo was the same kind of force fighting the same way. The sentence on the card, that in the phalanx it was the spear and not the sword that first decided who would stand, has both a negative and a positive side at Baipo. The negative is Song Jingang at Jiexiu, who formed his line seven li long outside the town; once a formation is stretched that far it breaks, the continuous face of thrusting spears is lost, and the collapse began there. The positive is the Tang army in Quexugu, fighting eight engagements in a single day, its men two days without food and three days without taking off their war coats, and still able to hold its order through the column and the cooperation of foot and horse. Besides the long spear and the lance, the Tang carried horizontal sabres at the waist for the rider to fight and cut with on horseback; crossbowmen and archers covered the field of fire from the rear ranks; the bronze chest protector known as Mingguang armour, in use since the reign of Emperor Wu of Han, marked the heavy infantry, while helmets and leather armour were the general equipment. The Han army followed the Sui pattern in the main, the strength of its horse lying in the Turkish fashion of man and beast both armoured and in the speed of the charge. Siege machines play no prominent part in the record of Baipo; both sides won by trenching, sealing and harassing the supply road with horse. On the logistic side the Han army had 'no stores, and lived on what it plundered', and living on plunder was exactly the point on which the Tang blockade pressed. Horses, wagons and grain moved along the official roads of Hedong; it is about four hundred li from Taiyuan to Baipo and about seven hundred li from Baipo to the line of Longmen Pass, and the distance was itself part of the arithmetic of this war.
tactics: 柏壁之戰的戰術主軸是三步：閉營、斷糧、追擊。李世民初屯柏壁時判斷漢軍「軍無蓄積，以虜掠為資」，遂閉營不出，積薪節食以老敵，等宋金剛糧盡自退，而不是在對方士氣正盛的時候硬碰硬。與此同時，唐軍用兩隻手去掐斷漢軍的呼吸：一是派張德政襲殺黃子英這名專司糧道的將領，二是趁漢軍主力在外，由秦武通取蒲坂，迫王行本出降，把河東境內唯一可援的一點拔掉。外線上，唐軍不與宋金剛的大隊糾纏，而是抓住分兵出來的騎兵打：美良川一役，殷開山、秦叔寶設伏，斬殺漢軍二千餘人；尉遲恭又秘密率精騎東援蒲坂，李世民偵知後親率精兵三千疾馳安邑截擊，又打散了他一次。兩擊得手，漢軍外線的耳目與骨頭都被拆掉，柏壁的對峙才轉向追擊。等到宋金剛糧盡退兵，唐軍咬住不放，經呂州、高壁嶺追入介休與霍縣之間的雀鼠谷，兩晝夜不眠不休，一日之內連打八戰而皆捷，斬殺俘虜上萬，士卒二日未進食、三日未脫戰袍。谷道狹窄，漢軍騎兵無法展開，正合唐軍以步卒長矛結陣、迫其下馬的長處。最後一戰在介休城西：宋金剛列陣七里，李世勣等先出，稍卻以誘其全軍壓上，李世民自將精騎繞到陣後猛擊其側背，兩面夾攻，宋軍遂崩。回馬槊與長矛的近身格鬥，此刻集中在潰兵之間。
tacticsEn: The tactical spine of Baipo was three steps: close the camp, cut the food, and pursue. When Li Shimin first took up position at Baipo he judged that the Han army had 'no stores and lived on plunder', so he shut his camp and did not fight, hoarding firewood and food to wear the enemy down until Song Jingang should break off for want of grain, rather than trading blows while the enemy's spirits were high. At the same time the Tang took the Han army by the throat with both hands: one was to send Zhangdezheng to strike down Huang Ziying, the officer in charge of the supply road; the other was to take advantage of the Han main body being away, have Qin Wutong seize Puzhang and force Wang Xingben to surrender, so as to pull out the one place in Hedong from which help could come. On the flanks the Tang refused to be entangled with Song Jingang's main host and instead struck at the horse that came out on detached service: at Meiliangchuan Yin Kaishan and Qin Shubao ambushed and cut down more than two thousand Han men; Yuchi Gong then rode secretly with picked horse to the east to relieve Puzhang, and Li Shimin, learning of it, led three thousand of his own men at speed to Anyi and cut him up again. With these two blows the eyes and the bones of the Han outer line were broken, and only then did the deadlock at Baipo turn into pursuit. When Song Jingang finally broke off for want of food the Tang held on to him: through Luzhou and Gaobiling they followed him into Quexugu, between Jiexiu and Huoxian, two days and nights without rest, eight engagements in a single day and all of them won, more than ten thousand of the enemy killed and taken, the men two days without food and three days without taking off their war coats. The valley road was narrow, the Han horse could not deploy, and that suited the Tang strength of tying the foot together with long spears and forcing the enemy to fight on foot. The last battle was fought outside Jiexiu: Song Jingang formed his line seven li long, Li Shiji and the others went out first and gave ground to draw the whole Han army forward, and Li Shimin took picked horse round behind the line to strike its flank and rear, so that the Han were caught between two attacks and broke. At that point the close work of the long lance and the long spear was all happening among the broken men.
data: 可核對的數字集中在幾處。漢軍南下的總數，舊唐書與資治通鑑都概稱三萬餘人：劉武周以宋金剛為西南道大行臺，率眾自太原南下，四月駐黃蛇嶺，五月取平遙，六月取介州。世民自請領精兵三萬，高祖准許並親自送行。反擊階段的數字更清楚：美良川一役，斬殺漢軍二千餘人；李世民率兵三千趨安邑截擊尉遲恭；宋金剛退保介休時，兵力約二萬，於城西列陣七里。追擊戰的戰果是八戰皆捷，斬殺俘虜上萬；士卒二日未進食、三日未脫戰袍。距離與時間也算得出來：長安至柏壁約七百里，柏壁至太原約四百里；十一月起兵屯柏壁，到次年四月追至雀鼠谷，對峙約五個月。戰前的敗績同樣有數可查：車騎將軍張達在榆次外全軍覆沒，姜寶誼、李仲文兩度被俘，裴寂在介休外潰散，李元吉棄晉陽，晉州、絳州、潞州相繼失守，關中一度議棄河東。這些數字說明一點：漢軍的優勢在兵數與騎兵，唐軍的優勢在精騎、封鎖與追擊，而五個月的對峙消耗掉的正是漢軍最缺的東西——糧食；宋金剛糧盡退兵那天，戰局的天平就已經傾斜了。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked gather in a few places. The total of the Han host that moved south is given in both the Old Book of Tang and the Comprehensive Mirror as more than thirty thousand men: Liu Wuzhou made Song Jingang Director of the Southwest Circuit and led the mass of his troops down from Bingzhou, halting at Huangshe Ridge in the fourth month, taking Pingyao in the fifth and Jiezhou in the sixth. Li Shimin asked for thirty thousand picked troops and the founding emperor granted them and saw him off in person. The figures for the counter-attack are clearer still: at Meiliangchuan more than two thousand Han men were killed; Li Shimin led three thousand men to Anyi to intercept Yuchi Gong; when Song Jingang fell back on Jiexiu he had about twenty thousand men and formed his line seven li long on the west of the town. The result of the pursuit was eight engagements, all won, with more than ten thousand of the enemy killed and taken; the men went two days without food and three days without taking off their war coats. Distance and time can be reckoned as well: about seven hundred li from Chang'an to Baipo and about four hundred li from Baipo to Taiyuan; the army was in position at Baipo from the eleventh month and only reached Quexugu in the fourth month of the following year, so the deadlock ran about five months. The defeats before the battle can be checked in the same way: the Commander of Chariot and Horse Zhang Da was wiped out outside Jiexiu, Jiang Baoyi and Li Zhongwen were taken captive twice, Pei Ji broke up outside Jiezhou, Li Yuanji abandoned Jinyang, Jinzhou, Jiangzhou and Luzhou fell in turn, and Guanzhong came close to abandoning Hedong. These figures make one point: the Han advantage lay in numbers and in horse, the Tang advantage in picked horse, in blockade and in pursuit, and what the five months of deadlock wore down was precisely the thing the Han army lacked, grain. On the day Song Jingang withdrew for want of food the balance of the battle had already tipped.
cause: 打起上來有隋末的大背景，也有武德二年的具體利害計算。隋亡之後，劉武周以馬步都尉起兵河東，十餘年間聚兵據地，靠的既是關中群雄彼此混戰給出的空隙，也是北方突厥的撐腰；李淵起兵太原，兩人同在一處根基上，李家能立國，靠的正是先據太原、進取關中。劉武周要的是把唐的根基抽掉，李家不能容忍的也是這件事。時機上，武德二年唐廷正同時對付河北的竇建德、洛陽的王世充與陝北的梁師都，河東防務相對空虛，漢軍才得以在四月至九月連取榆次、平遙、介州、太原，把關中的門戶洞開。九月太原陷落，關中震駭，高祖的判斷是「賊勢如此，難與爭鋒，宜棄大河以東，謹守關西而已」，這是純粹按地盤損益算的帳。世民的算法不同：河東是王業所基，一旦放棄，關中就只剩一個孤立的關隘；於是他上表爭取領兵三萬，並自請與劉武周勢不兩立。外交上唐廷也曾試圖在劉武周與梁師都之間落子：高祖遣書約二人斷絕河東沙漠以相接應，把北方兩股割據勢力聯成一體再對付，結果書到而事不成。於是只剩一條路：靠戰場上的時間、封鎖與追擊，把劉武周的優勢一點一點耗掉。
causeEn: The fighting began against the background of the end of Sui, and for concrete reasons of advantage in the second year of Wude. After Sui fell, Liu Wuzhou rose in Hedong as a Commander of Horse and Foot and spent more than ten years gathering troops and holding ground, helped both by the gaps left by the rival warlords of Guanzhong fighting one another and by the support of the Turks to the north. Li Yuan rose at Taiyuan, the two men stood on the same foundation, and the Li family's ability to found a state rested precisely on taking Taiyuan first and moving on to Guanzhong. What Liu Wuzhou wanted was to pull the ground from under the Tang, and the Tang could not tolerate it either. As for timing, in the second year of Wude the court was dealing at once with Dou Jiande in Hebei, Wang Shichong at Luoyang and Liang Shidu in northern Shaanxi, and the Hedong defences were comparatively thin; that was how the Han army was able to take Jiexiu, Pingyao, Jiezhou and Taiyuan in succession from April to September and open the gate of Guanzhong. When Taiyuan fell in September and Guanzhong was shaken, the emperor's judgement was that 'the enemy is in such strength that it cannot be matched; the best course is to give up everything east of the Yellow River and guard the west of the passes carefully' - an account drawn purely from the balance sheet of territory. Li Shimin's arithmetic was different: Hedong was the foundation of the royal enterprise, and once it was given up Guanzhong would be nothing but an isolated pass. So he memorialised to be allowed three ten-thousand men, and swore with Liu Wuzhou that the two would not both live. On the diplomatic side the court also tried to play between Liu Wuzhou and Liang Shudu: the emperor sent a letter proposing that the two cut the desert route in Hedong so as to support each other, joining the two northern separatist regimes against the Tang; the letter arrived and nothing came of it. One road was left: to spend time, to blockade and to pursue, and so wear down Liu Wuzhou's advantage piece by piece.
impact: 這一役的結果改變了唐的戰略版圖，也改變了北方的人事。劉武周經營近十年的割據政權一朝瓦解，河東的太原、晉、絳三州重歸唐室，太原光復；唐廷從此不只是在關中守住一道關隘，而是握著河東這個人口、物產與兵源的倉庫。唐軍在戰中收得尉遲恭、尋相兩員悍將及其部眾，等於把北方的騎戰經驗與一批精騎裝進自己的軍中；白毦兵一類精銳部隊的打法也在這一串戰鬥裡成型，兩年後凌煙閣二十四功臣的班底，多數是在這幾年裡因戰功聚合起來的。對北方草原勢力而言，劉武周與宋金剛相繼死在突厥手上，說明唐廷已經把河東從突厥的勢力範圍裡切斷，北方的主要威脅由唐轉為突厥本身，兩國在西北的角力從此延續到貞觀年間。兵學上的影響更為持久：此役的「閉營待其糧盡、乘勝追擊不與其喘息」被資治通鑑卷一百八十七、一百八十八與舊唐書本紀詳細記下，成為唐代講兵者常引用的案例；雀鼠谷一日八戰、士卒二日不食三日不解甲這類細節，因正史保存得完整，成為後世描述追擊戰最常引用的段落之一。而就兵器本身而言，柏壁的記錄也把方陣的兩面都擺了出來：站在哪裡、由誰來站、能不能在縱隊與亂軍之中保持縱深，決定了長矛能不能刺到人。
impactEn: The result of this campaign changed both the strategic map of the Tang and the personnel of the north. The separatist regime Liu Wuzhou had spent nearly ten years building collapsed in a single stroke; Bingzhou, Jinzhou and Jiangzhou in Hedong returned to the Tang house, and Taiyuan was recovered. From that moment the court was no longer merely holding a pass in Guanzhong: it was holding Hedong, the storehouse of population, produce and recruits. By taking Yuchi Gong and Xun Xiang and their men the Tang army put the northern art of mounted fighting and a body of picked horse into its own ranks, and the way of fighting used by picked units such as the White Guard was formed in this string of engagements; the greater part of the twenty-four meritorious officials later inscribed in the Lingyan Pavilion were gathered together in these years on the strength of battlefield service. As for the powers of the steppe, the fact that Liu Wuzhou and Song Jingang both died in Turkic hands showed that the court had cut Hedong away from the sphere of Turkic influence: the principal northern threat became the Turks themselves, and the rivalry of the two states in the north-west ran on into the Zhenguan years. The effect on the art of war was the most durable of all. The method used here - shut in the camp and wait for the enemy's grain to run out, then pursue without giving him a chance to breathe - was set down in detail in the Comprehensive Mirror in volumes one hundred and eighty-seven and one hundred and eighty-eight and in the annals of the Old Book of Tang, and became a case constantly cited by Tang writers on warfare. Details such as the eight engagements in a single day at Quexugu and the men two days without food and three days without taking off their war coats, preserved so completely in the official histories, became one of the most frequently quoted passages in later accounts of the pursuit battle. As to the weapon itself, the record of Baipo also sets out both sides of the phalanx: where a man stands, who stands there, and whether the depth can be kept in a marching column or in a broken melee determine whether the long spear can reach a man at all.
result: 結果是唐軍完勝，而且是一種艱苦的完勝。宋金剛在介休城西列陣七里，兵敗之後率眾北走，兩萬餘人散盡；尉遲恭、尋相等率部眾降唐，唐軍不追宋金剛而先收降將，等於用政治手段截斷了漢軍最後的指揮核心。宋金剛退至上谷，為突厥所擒，遭腰斬；劉武周棄太原北走突厥，泣對苑君璋說「不用君言，以至於此」，不久亦為突厥所殺，漢政權連同北方兩名主將一起從此消失。太原光復，太原、晉、絳三州歸唐，唐廷在高祖一朝終於拿回了河東，也才有餘力在武德三年先收洛陽王世充、再破河北竇建德。代價同樣記在帳上：榆次、介休一役的接連失利，張達全軍覆沒，姜寶誼、李仲文被俘殺害，裴寂大潰，太原失守，關中一度要放棄河東；而追擊到最後的士卒，二日未進食、三日未脫戰袍，柏壁與雀鼠谷之間的五百餘里，是這樣走出來的。回到卡面那件斯巴達長矛：它沒有出現在這場戰爭的任何一份名單上，但它留下的那句話在這裡得到了反面印證——介休城西那條長達七里的陣線站不住，長矛的刺擊面一旦斷開便無從施力；而唐軍在谷道裡靠步卒結陣與騎兵迂迴配合站住了陣腳，才等到追擊的那一天。方陣決定誰站得住，站得住之後，還要看誰先斷糧、誰先動彈不得。
resultEn: The result was a complete Tang victory, and a hard-won one. Song Jingang formed his line seven li long outside Jiexiu and, after the defeat, carried his men north with more than twenty thousand of them scattered; Yuchi Gong, Xun Xiang and the rest came over with their men, and the Tang army, instead of pursuing Song Jingang, first took the surrendered commanders, cutting the last directing core of the Han army by political means. Song Jingang withdrew to Shanggu, was taken by the Turks and was cut in two; Liu Wuzhou abandoned Taiyuan and fled north to the Turks, weeping before Yuan Junzhang and saying 'I did not take your words, and I came to this', and was killed by them soon after, so that the Han regime and its two northern commanders disappeared from the scene together. Taiyuan was recovered and Bingzhou, Jinzhou and Jiangzhou returned to the Tang; in the reign of the founding emperor the court finally got Hedong back, and only then had it the strength to take Wang Shichong at Luoyang and break Dou Jiande in Hebei in the third year of Wude. The cost is entered on the same page: the run of defeats at Jiexiu and Jiezhou, Zhang Da's whole force destroyed, Jiang Baoyi and Li Zhongwen taken and killed, Pei Ji's army broken, the loss of Taiyuan, and a moment when Guanzhong was ready to give up Hedong; and the men who pursued to the end, two days without food and three days without taking off their war coats, covered the more than five hundred li between Baipo and Quexugu in that state. Returning to the Spartan long spear on the card: it appears on no list of this war at all, but the sentence it carries is here confirmed from the other side. The line seven li long outside Jiexiu could not stand; once the face of the thrusting spear is broken it has nothing to work with. The Tang, by tying the foot together in the valley road and working the horse round to strike in flank, did hold their order, and so lived to reach the day of pursuit. The phalanx decides who can stand; but once a man is standing, it is still a question of who cuts the food first and who is the first to be unable to move.
